Issued at 240 PM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

Through Tonight...A nor'easter positioned near the Mid Atlantic 
has continued to gradually lift northward, with high pressure 
slowly building across the southeastern US. The pressure gradient 
across the Florida peninsula has slowly slackened through the day,
with north-northeast winds remaining around 10 to 15 mph, 
strongest along the coast and enhanced locally by the diffuse east
coast sea breeze. Aside from some fair weather cumulus, skies are
mostly sunny with drier air helping to limit shower development. 
This is anticipated to persist into the evening and overnight 
hours, with no mentionable rain or storm chances in the forecast. 
Afternoon temperatures remain on track to peak in the low to mid 
80s, with low humidity keeping conditions mild. Tonight, 
temperatures are forecast to fall into the 60s, coolest across the
interior west of I-95. At the beaches, a high risk of rip 
currents will persist through the remainder of today into the 
overnight hours, along with breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet. 
Entering the surf is not advised.

Sunday-Monday...As the nor'easter continue to lift northward and 
barrel into the New England and Mid Atlantic region this weekend, 
locally, surface high pressure and a dry air mass will continue to
settle across east central Florida. The pressure gradient 
weakens, with light and variable winds anticipated Sunday into 
Monday, though areas along the coast may become more onshore 
during the afternoon hours with the development of a weak, diffuse
east coast sea breeze. Rain and storm chances are anticipated to 
remain near zero each day as the drier air mass helps limit 
development, with mostly sunny skies forecast through the period. 
Temperatures are forecast to remain seasonable on Sunday afternoon
in the mid 80s, warming slightly into the mid to upper 80s on 
Monday. Overnight temperatures remain in the 60s. Overall, 
conditions look favorable and even pleasant across east central 
Florida over the next couple of days.

While the weather will be favorable across the area, if heading 
to the beaches, conditions won't be quite as favorable surf-wise. 
Lingering seas will produce poor to hazardous beach conditions, 
with a high risk of rip currents continuing into Sunday and likely
Monday. Rough surf with breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet will 
continue on Sunday, falling to 2 to 3 feet on Monday. Entering the
ocean through Monday is strongly discouraged due to the poor 
conditions. 

Tuesday-Friday...A broad mid-level trough shifts southward across
the southeastern US and towards the Florida peninsula mid to late
next week. At the surface, moisture slowly begins to increase as 
a broad, weak disturbance lifts northeastward across Cuba, with 
another broad, weak disturbance lifting north across the Gulf late
next week. This will translate to increasing rain and storm 
chances locally, increasing from 20-40% on Tuesday from Orlando 
southward to 30-70% Wednesday onward areawide. Onshore flow will 
prevail through the extended period, becoming enhanced along the 
coast as a diffuse east coast sea breeze develops and moves 
inland. As mentioned, storm development will be possible with 
activity, with lightning, gusty winds, and heavy downpours all 
possible. Exact storm threats will become clearer as time 
progresses. Activity is expected to follow a somewhat diurnal 
pattern, with highest coverage in the afternoon and early evening 
hours slowly diminishing into the late evening and overnight 
hours. Ongoing development across the local Atlantic waters will 
be possible. The persistent onshore flow combined with the 
increasing moisture will help the local air mass become slightly 
warmer, with temperatures anticipated to be near to slightly above
normal values for this time of year. The warmest temperatures 
will primarily be focused across the interior during the afternoon
hours.
